subject: history_social
passage: Napoleon Bonaparte is often remembered as an unusually short man, and his name has even been attached to the idea that small men seek power to make up for their size. That image rests on shaky ground. At his death his height was recorded as five feet two inches, but in French units, which were longer than British ones; in British measure he stood about five feet seven, average or slightly above for a Frenchman of his day. British cartoonists, who mocked him as a tiny, tantrum-prone figure, helped fix the image in the public mind.
stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

choices.A: It presents a popular image of a historical figure and then explains why that image is misleading.
choices.B: It explains how French units of length differed from the British units used at the time.
choices.C: It argues that British cartoonists deliberately spread false information to win a war.
choices.D: It describes Napoleon's rise to power and then explains the sources of his ambition.

explanation.why: The first sentence describes how Napoleon "is often remembered": as very short. The second says this image "rests on shaky ground," and the rest explains why: a confusion between French and British units, plus mocking British cartoons that spread the image. The text moves from a popular belief to the reasons it is mistaken.
explanation.A: Correct. The text sets up the belief that Napoleon was very short and then explains the measurement mix-up and the cartoons behind it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The difference in units is one piece of evidence used to correct the image, not the structure of the whole text.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says cartoonists "helped fix the image" but says nothing about deliberate lies or winning a war; this goes beyond the text.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text mentions the idea that small men seek power but never describes Napoleon's rise or the sources of his ambition.
